title: Optimal volume management and outcome in free flap surgery
summary:
Large wounds or areas where soft tissue has been lost sometimes cannot heal on their own. In these cases, surgeons may perform an operation called a free flap transfer. During this procedure, healthy tissue, together with its blood vessels, is taken from one part of the body (for example, the thigh) and moved to the area that needs reconstruction. The blood vessels are then connected to blood vessels at the new site so that the transferred tissue continues to receive a blood supply and can heal properly.
These operations usually take many hours. During surgery, the body may react with inflammation, which is a normal response to major surgery. However, if this response becomes too strong, it may affect the patient's recovery and increase the risk of complications. It is not yet fully understood why this happens or whether a stronger inflammatory response causes patients to need more fluids and medications to support their blood pressure during the operation. It is also unclear whether this may increase the risk of problems such as failure of the transferred tissue or other complications.
The OptiVOL study is looking at information from patients who underwent a free flap transfer at Unfallkrankenhaus Berlin between 2023 and 2025. This is a retrospective study, which means that no additional examinations or treatments will be carried out. Instead, researchers will analyse information that has already been recorded in the hospital's electronic medical records as part of routine care.
The study will examine how much intravenous fluid and blood pressure support medication patients needed during their operation to keep their circulation stable. It will also analyse routine blood test results that provide information about inflammation and the body's metabolism.
The researchers will then look for possible links between the body's inflammatory response and the amount of fluids and medications required during surgery. The results of this study may help doctors better understand how to care for patients undergoing free flap surgery and may contribute to improving treatment for future patients.

interventions.name:
The OptiVOL project is designed as a retrospective observational study. Clinical data from patients who underwent elective free flap transfer for soft tissue reconstruction at the Unfallkrankenhaus Berlin gGmbH (ukb) between 2023 and 2025 will be collected and analysed statistically.
